paper.title: Nearly Optimal Sampling Algorithms for Combinatorial Pure Exploration

unmapped: goal is to identify the subset in a known family F of subsets of the arms with maximum total mean (combinatorial pure exploration); each sample is from a single base arm
the learner knows the family F
settings.definition_quote: In a \combibandit\ instance $\combiband=(S,\subsetfam)$, we are given a set $S$ of $n$ arms. Each arm $a \in S$ is associated with a Gaussian reward distribution with unit variance and an unknown mean $\mu_a$. We are also given a family of subsets $\subsetfam$ ... Our goal is to find with probability at least $1-\delta$, a subset in $\subsetfam$ with the maximum total mean using as few samples as possible. We assume that there is a unique subset with the maximum total mean.

unmapped: goal: identify which of a known collection of disjoint answer sets in R^n contains the mean profile; each answer set disjoint from the closure of the union of the others
settings.definition_quote: An instance of the general sampling problem is a pair $\inst = (\armseq,\anssetcol)$, where $\armseq$ is a sequence of $n$ Gaussian arms each with unit variance, and $\anssetcol$ is a collection of answer sets, each of which is a subset of $\real^n$. ... The goal is to identify with probability $1- \delta$ the unique set in $\anssetcol$ that contains $\mean$, while using as few samples as possible.

algorithms.name: Random-subset sampling tester for ball instance (Theorem C.2)

symbols.Low_C: optimal value of convex program (eq:gklowdef): min sum tau_i s.t. sum_{i in O xor A} 1/tau_i <= (mu(O)-mu(A))^2 for all A in F

source.label: theo:LB
source.quote: Let $\combiband = (S,\subsetfam)$ be an instance of $\combibandit$. Let $\gklow(\combiband)$ be the optimal value of the convex program~\eqref{eq:gklowdef}. Then for any $\delta \in (0,0.1)$ and $\delta$-correct algorithm $\alg$ for $\combibandit$, $\alg$ takes $\Omega(\gklow(\combiband) \ln \delta^{-1})$ samples in expectation on $\combiband$.

results.notes: Instance-wise lower bound. Theorem 1.7 shows Low_C >= H_C = sum_i Delta_i^-2.

symbols.Low_C: optimal value of the instance lower-bound convex program for Best-Set
symbols.Delta_set: gap between total mean of optimal set and second-best set in F

source.label: theo:naive-upperb
source.quote: There is a $\delta$-correct algorithm for $\combibandit$ that takes $$O\left( \gklow(\combiband)\ln\delta^{-1} + \gklow(\combiband)\ln\Delta^{-1}\left(\ln\ln\Delta^{-1} + \ln|\subsetfam|\right) \right)$$ samples on an instance $\combiband = (S,\subsetfam)$ in expectation, where $\Delta$ denote the gap between the set with the second largest total mean in $\subsetfam$ and the optimal set $\ansset$.

results.notes: Computation polynomial in n and |F| when F given explicitly (Remark 4.1).

conditions: m <= 2^{cn} for a universal constant c
holds on an infinite sequence of n-arm instances with Low_C -> infinity

source.label: theo:worst-case-lowb-comb
source.quote: (i) For $\delta \in (0,0.1)$, two positive integers $n$ and $m \le 2^{c n}$ where $c$ is a universal constant,, and every $\delta$-correct algorithm $\alg$ for \combibandit, there exists an infinite sequence of $n$-arm instances ... such that $\alg$ takes at least $\Omega( \gklow(\combiband_k) \cdot (\ln \delta^{-1}+\ln |\subsetfam_k|))$ samples in expectation on each $\combiband_k$, $|\subsetfam_k| = m$ for all $k$

results.notes: Part (ii) shows instance-specific delta-correct algorithms achieve O(Low_C*poly(ln n, ln 1/delta)) on each such instance; not recorded separately (poly unspecified).

symbols.Delta_set: gap between optimal and second-best set

conditions: family F admits an efficient maximization oracle and a pseudo-polynomial algorithm for the exact version (e.g. spanning trees, bipartite matchings, s-t paths)

source.label: theo:effi-comb
source.quote: For any family of \combibandit{} instances that admits efficient maximization oracles and pseudo-polynomial algorithms, there is a $\delta$-correct algorithm for this instance family that takes $$O\left(\gklow(\combiband)\ln\delta^{-1} + \gklow(\combiband)\ln^2\Delta^{-1}\left(\ln\ln\Delta^{-1} + \ln|\subsetfam|\right)\right)$$ samples ... Moreover, the algorithm runs in polynomial time with respect to the expected sample complexity.

results.notes: Polynomial time in n and the sample complexity.

symbols.Low_I: optimal value of LP (eq:genlbdef): min sum tau_i s.t. sum_i (nu_i-mu_i)^2 tau_i >= 1 for all nu in Alt(O)
symbols.Delta_I: minimum Euclidean distance from the mean profile to any alternative mean profile

source.label: theo:general-upperb
source.quote: There is a $\delta$-correct algorithm for $\generalbandit$ that takes $$O(\gklow(\inst) \; (\ln\delta^{-1} + n^3 + n\ln\Delta^{-1}))$$ samples on any instance $\inst = (\armseq, \anssetcol)$ in expectation, where $$\Delta = \inf_{\tilmean\in\alt(\ansset)}\twonorm{\mean-\tilmean}$$

results.notes: n arms mapped to K. Requires solving an LP with possibly infinitely many constraints; computation not discussed.

symbols.Low_I: instance lower-bound LP value for General-Samp

source.label: theo:genlb
source.quote: Suppose $\delta\in(0,0.1)$ and $\inst$ is an instance of \generalbandit. Any $\delta$-correct algorithm for \generalbandit{} takes $\Omega(\gklow(\inst)\ln\delta^{-1})$ samples in expectation on $\inst$.

results.notes: Paper notes the proof is similar to Garivier & Kaufmann 2016.

symbols.Low_I: instance lower-bound LP value for General-Samp

conditions: holds on an infinite sequence of n-arm instances with |answer collection| = O(1) and Low_I -> infinity

source.label: theo:lower-bound-general
source.quote: For $\delta \in (0,0.1)$, a positive integer $n$ and every $\delta$-correct algorithm $\alg$ for the general sampling problem, there exists an infinite sequence of $n$-arm instances ... such that $\alg$ takes at least $\Omega( \gklow(\inst_k) \cdot (\ln \delta^{-1}+ n))$ samples in expectation on each $\inst_k$, $|\anssetcol_k| =O(1)$ for all $k$, and $\gklow(\inst_k)$ goes to infinity.

results.notes: Second part: for each such instance an instance-specific delta-correct algorithm achieves O(Low_I*log(1/delta)); not recorded separately.

symbols.r_ball: radius r <= 1 separating the answer set {u} from {v : ||u-v||_2 >= r}

conditions: answer collection is {{u}, {v: ||u-v||_2 >= r}} with r <= 1
bound is on the instance whose mean profile is u

source.label: theo:ball-case
source.quote: For a positive integer $n$, a positive real number $r \le 1$ and a vector $u \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we define $\anssetcol = \{ \{u\}, \{ v \in \mathbb{R}^n : \|u-v\|_2 \ge r \}  \}$. There is a $\delta$-correct algorithm for $\generalbandit$ which takes $O\left(n \ln^2 n \cdot r^{-2} \cdot (\ln n + \ln \delta^{-1}) \cdot \ln\delta^{-1}\right)$ samples in expectation on the instance $\inst = (S, \anssetcol)$, where $S$ is a sequence of arms with mean profile $u$.

results.notes: Special instance of General-Samp; used to prove Theorem 1.9(ii).
